machine: MacBook Air, Intel i5-5350U @ 1.80GHz, 4 logical cpus, 8 GB, macOS 21.6.0 — a shared development laptop, not a dedicated host
storage: internal Apple NVMe SSD, APFS, volume 90% full, shared with the OS
host_disclosures: load average 2.25 > 1 before the run started
load average climbed 3.42 during the run (2.25 to 5.67), more than the 1.5 this benchmark can account for, so other work joined it
9.48 GB free on the fixture volume < 20 GB; a filesystem near capacity measurably slows file creation, which is most of this requirement's tail

verdict.measured_on: the worst repeat, not the median across repeats

attribution: Cryptography is not the cost. SHA-256 and AES-GCM over a record are 0.03 ms together, while creating one file measured p50 0.2162 ms against 0.0083 ms for a write to an already-open descriptor. So the append path creates no file at all: both journals are held open and every payload goes into one append-only encrypted blob.
A single file creation has a p99 of 2.2977 ms on this machine, which is why no design that creates a file per record can meet a 1 ms p99 here, however fast its hashing.

The remaining tail is not per-record work: an open-descriptor write has a p99 of 0.0382 ms against the chain arm's 0.6602 ms. What it is instead is reported above and not guessed at — if the GC share of the slowest samples is low, the outliers are the operating system, and the maxima here routinely exceed anything the per-record work could account for.

Across 3 repeats the full arm's p99 ranged up to 2.6065 ms and the filesystem baseline moved with it, so this machine is not the reference environment NFR-01 now requires. The p50 and p95 are the stable figures.

Garbage collection is measured, not inferred: 2021 pause(s) totalling 26362.5 ms during the full arm, overlapping 20% of its slowest one per cent of samples. The recorder was verified against a deliberate allocation storm in this same run (8 pauses seen), so a low number here is a measurement rather than a lost one — an earlier version reported zero because it disconnected the observer before the asynchronous entries could be delivered.
